title: A retinoic acid autoregulatory loop governing prefrontal-motor arealization.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Found GEO series GSE325427 (34 samples, human + mouse, public 2026-07-15, BioProject PRJNA1438418) via GEO search; the Nature paper and the preprint PDF still say 'GSEXXXXXX'. Downloaded and parsed all six human mid-fetal dlPFC (dorsolateral prefrontal cortex) CUT&Tag peak files: MEIS2 54,237, RARA 19,426, RARB 10,422, RXRG 36,345, H3K27ac 58,911, H3K4me3 23,420 peaks; 3-column BED with no score column and 0 duplicate rows. Overlaps: 30% of RARA peaks and 30% of RARB peaks fall in H3K4me3 (promoter-mark) peaks; 48% of RARA peaks fall in H3K27ac peaks. Opened the Meis2 cKO (conditional knockout) bulk RNA-seq workbook: 25,239 genes x 3 control + 3 cKO counts, and a 19,864-row DESeq2 sheet whose top hit is Xist (log2FC 10.7). Counted 50,740 snRNA barcodes across 4 human donors. Read GEO filelist: the per-sample files are ATAC fragments (1.4-3.7 GB each) and mtx matrices; the RAW tar is 19 GB.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Donor ages (PCW 18-22 multiome, 19-23 CUT&Tag), the genome build, the peak caller, the claim that RAR/RXR sites sit near axonogenesis genes, and the SCENIC+ regulatory network all come from the bioRxiv preprint text (10.64898/2025.12.23.696038). The Nature version is paywalled and I did not read it; the NCBI PubMed-to-PMC link (PMC13192659) points to a different, citing Bhaduri-lab preprint.

a1_downloadable.note: Checked: GEO GSE325427 is public; peak BEDs and the DEG xlsx downloaded without login.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Checked: for the sequence-to-binding task, the label is membership in a deposited peak file. Negatives must be sampled from non-peak genome, which is standard but still a design choice. No signal or score column exists, so only a binary label is possible.

a3_inputs_present.note: The inputs are DNA sequences under hg38 coordinates. This needs one reference-genome download (about 1 GB), not thousands of lookups. The build is inferred from chr names and the preprint and is not stated in the files.

a4_units_stated.note: The label is binary (peak or no peak), so no units are needed. BigWig signal units are undocumented, but we wouldn't use them.

a5_enough_rows.note: Checked: the smallest factor set (RARB) has 10,422 peaks; MEIS2 has 54,237. Caveat: there are only 2 donors per factor, merged into one peak set.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~1 GB (hg38 FASTA plus <2 MB of peak BEDs)
a6_fits_laptop.note: The peaks are tiny. The 19 GB RAW tar and the multi-GB ATAC fragments are not needed for this task.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: The preprint gives no peak counts to compare against. The GEO sample list (4 human multiome donors, 2 CUT&Tag donors per mark, 3 vs 3 bulk RNA-seq) matches the preprint's methods.

a8_label_provenance.note: The label is a peak call: a computational threshold on a direct CUT&Tag measurement, not another model's prediction. Risk: TF CUT&Tag is known to bleed into open chromatin (30% of RARA peaks overlap H3K4me3), so some 'binding' may really be accessibility.

B1.why: One BED per factor (checked); must join to the hg38 FASTA and sample background regions.

B2.why: All six BED.gz files parsed first try with pandas (checked).

B3.why: Same lab and assay, but only binary merged peaks, with no signal score to compare factors (checked).

B4.why: No censored values; the labels are binary peak membership.

B5.why: 0 duplicate intervals in any peak file (checked).

B6.why: Three bare columns. Genome build, peak caller and replicate merging are only in the preprint methods.

C1.why: The 'binding versus merely open chromatin' question is informative either way, but a plain binding predictor needs to beat motif scans.

C2.why: Strong open sequence-to-chromatin models exist (ChromBPNet); none are trained on fetal-brain RAR/RXR binding.

C3.why: Diversity angle: fetal human brain tissue rather than cell lines. Weak beyond that.

C4.why: CUT&Tag on mid-fetal human cortex is scarce and costly, but the predictions wouldn't replace it.

C5.why: Obvious baselines (GC content, DR1/DR5 motif scan), but no published number on this data.

D1.why: Open DNA language models (DNABERT-2, Nucleotide Transformer) take 500 bp peak sequences directly.

D2.why: About 150k sequences of ~500 bp; embeddings can be cached once on CPU.

D3.why: Licences not checked here; Nucleotide Transformer is believed non-commercial. Fine for research.

E1.why: Hold out whole chromosomes, a standard split for genomic sequence models.

E2.why: 22 autosomes give many held-out groups; the peaks span all chromosomes (checked).

E3.why: GC-content and motif-count logistic regression are trivial to compute.

E4.why: Only merged peaks are deposited; replicate agreement needs reprocessing of raw reads.

E5.why: DR5/DR1 motifs should enrich in RARA/RARB peaks and TGACAG in MEIS2 peaks. Not yet tested.

E6.why: Label shuffle, dinucleotide-shuffled sequences and GC-only models are all runnable.

E7.why: ReMap/ENCODE cell-line RAR/RXR ChIP-seq gives an independent binding set on hg38 coordinates.

E8.why: The paper reports enrichments, not a predictive number to reproduce.

G1.why: Genomic coordinates only; the build (hg38 implied) isn't written in the files.

G2.why: ReMap / ENCODE TF ChIP-seq, joinable by interval overlap on hg38.

G3.why: Interval overlaps can be many-to-many; a collapse rule (any overlap) is easy.

G4.why: Asks whether fetal-brain RAR binding follows the cell-line grammar. A modest gain.

H1.why: Negatives are implicit (non-peak genome) and must be sampled.

H2.why: One lab, one region (dlPFC), 2 donors per factor, mid-fetal ages only.

H3.why: Claim can be stated precisely; see honest_claim_h3.

H4.why: Donor counts are in the preprint; the promoter bias of CUT&Tag isn't discussed.

I1.why: Developmental-neuroscience groups studying retinoic acid (e.g. Sestan lab); no named user of predictions.

I2.why: Could prioritise candidate RA-responsive enhancers or variants for reporter assays; marginal.

I3.why: AUPRC on held-out chromosomes roughly matches ranking candidate sites.

I4.why: A position weight matrix scan may perform nearly as well; that is itself the test.

J1.why: Real sequence modelling, chromosome splits and frozen-backbone transfer.

J2.why: Motif enrichment gives some sanity checking; chromatin biology needs domain input.

J3.why: The motif-enrichment and accessibility-bias check is a shareable result on day one.

J4.why: Roughly a 2-week project, not yet written down.

J5.why: Kill condition defined below; no date yet in NOTES.md.

existing_models.name: ChromBPNet (bias-factorised base-resolution sequence model of chromatin accessibility)
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported competitive with larger models on variant effects and pioneer TF binding across contexts (bioRxiv 2024.12.25.630221); evaluated on held-out chromosomes. Not trained on RAR/RXR CUT&Tag.

existing_models.name: Human Development Multiomic Atlas sequence models (Nature, s41586-026-10326-9)
existing_models.score_and_split: ChromBPNet models of fetal chromatin accessibility across 12 organs and 203 cell types; I saw the title and summary only, not the scores.

backbone.name: DNABERT-2 or Nucleotide Transformer (DNA language models), embeddings of 500 bp peak sequences
backbone.hardware: Laptop CPU; ~150k sequences, a few hours to embed
backbone.licence: Not checked; Nucleotide Transformer believed non-commercial

integration.partner_dataset: ReMap / ENCODE RARA, RXRA and MEIS ChIP-seq peaks in cell lines
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Do retinoic acid receptors in the fetal human prefrontal cortex bind the same sequence grammar as in cell lines, or does brain context recruit them to different sites?

controls.positive_control: DR5/DR1 direct-repeat motif enrichment in RARA/RARB peaks and MEIS TGACAG motif in MEIS2 peaks; the model should recover these in attribution maps.
controls.negative_control: Dinucleotide-shuffled peak sequences and shuffled labels must fall to the GC-content baseline.
controls.external_validation: ReMap/ENCODE cell-line RAR/RXR ChIP-seq peaks on hg38.

honest_claim_h3: Predicts which ~500 bp regions were called as RAR, RXR or MEIS2 CUT&Tag peaks in pooled mid-fetal dorsolateral prefrontal cortex from 2 donors, which partly reflects open chromatin rather than direct binding.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use DNA sequence to predict where retinoic acid receptors and MEIS2 bind in the developing human prefrontal cortex, beyond merely open chromatin.
plain_idea.train_on: About 500-letter DNA stretches: peaks for each factor (10,422 RARB to 54,237 MEIS2, counted) plus matched non-peak background regions.
plain_idea.predict: Whether a region was called a binding peak in CUT&Tag (an antibody-guided DNA-cutting assay) on mid-fetal human brain tissue from 2 donors.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: It tells developmental neuroscientists whether brain retinoic acid binding follows a known DNA grammar that could flag candidate enhancers and disease variants. A failure would show the peaks mostly track open chromatin.

more_or_better_data.why: Fetal human brain tissue for RAR/RXR binding is rare, but it is only 10k-54k merged peaks from 2 donors, whereas sequence models train on hundreds of ENCODE tracks.

confidence_score.why: No replicate-level processed peaks or signal scores are deposited, so per-site confidence can't be calibrated from the data.

models_beatable.why: ChromBPNet (2024) is strong and evaluated on held-out chromosomes, but it was not trained on brain RAR/RXR binding; a task-specific head could plausibly beat a generic model on this one task.

guaranteed_improvement.why: No accessible extra data measures the same factors in the same tissue with the same assay; ReMap cell-line ChIP-seq is a different assay and context.

label_elsewhere.sources: ReMap and ENCODE TF ChIP-seq include RARA/RXRA and MEIS factors in cell lines (known resources; not queried here).
label_elsewhere.why: Cell-line binding sets give a ready external test of whether a fetal-brain model generalises, or how far brain binding departs from cell lines.

risks: Repeated or duplicated genome sequence (segmental duplications, alt contigs present in the BEDs) can place near-identical regions in both train and test.
Background negatives that differ in GC content or promoter status from peaks let the model learn 'promoter vs not' rather than binding.
The TF peaks overlap H3K4me3/H3K27ac peaks (30-48% for RARA), so a model may learn open chromatin, which the same tissue's histone peaks already reveal.
Blacklist artefact regions (e.g. chr1:10,000 appears in every peak file) are shared across factors and inflate multi-task accuracy.
leakage_plan.split: Hold out whole chromosomes (e.g. chr8 and chr9 for test, chr10 for validation), built from column 0 of the BED files (seen); drop alt contigs and ENCODE blacklist regions.
checks: Train on GC content plus H3K27ac/H3K4me3 overlap alone and see how close it comes to the full model.
Restrict to H3K27ac-marked regions and ask whether the model still separates RAR-bound from unbound.
Shuffle labels and confirm AUPRC (area under the precision-recall curve) collapses to the positive rate.
Check the k-mer similarity of each test peak to its nearest training peak.
leakage_plan.verdict: Manageable. Chromosome splits are standard; the real danger is learning accessibility, not leakage across the split.

success_criteria.metric: AUPRC for RARA/RARB peaks versus H3K27ac-matched non-bound regions on held-out chromosomes, because the question is 'bound beyond open chromatin'.
success_criteria.baselines: Positive-class rate (dummy); a GC-content plus DR5/DR1 motif-count logistic regression; no published number exists.
success_criteria.success: AUPRC at least 0.10 above the motif-scan baseline on held-out chromosomes within the H3K27ac-matched set. The threshold is our choice, not derived from data.
success_criteria.kill: If RARA/RARB peaks show no DR5/DR1 enrichment over H3K27ac background, the label is accessibility, so stop.

ambitious.why: Publishes tissue-specific regulatory-grammar analyses; it would need a clear brain-specific RAR binding grammar validated against ReMap cell-line binding.

realistic.why: Fits a focused re-analysis showing whether fetal-brain RAR/RXR CUT&Tag binding is predictable from sequence beyond open chromatin.

fallback.why: A negative result (peaks mostly track accessibility) is still a useful caution about TF CUT&Tag in tissue.

pitch.headline: Rare RAR, RXR and MEIS2 binding maps from mid-fetal human prefrontal cortex: 10,422 to 54,237 peaks per factor, public on GEO.
pitch.what_makes_the_data_unusual: Six CUT&Tag peak sets from primary mid-fetal human brain tissue (checked), alongside histone marks from the same tissue. Retinoic acid receptor binding is usually profiled in cell lines.
pitch.the_win: A frozen DNA language model that separates RAR-bound from merely acetylated regions on held-out chromosomes, at least 0.10 AUPRC above a DR5/DR1 motif scan.
pitch.even_if_it_fails: We learn whether tissue TF CUT&Tag peaks are mostly open-chromatin bleed-through. 30% of RARA peaks already overlap promoter marks (checked).
pitch.who_wants_it: Groups studying retinoic acid signalling in cortical development (e.g. the Sestan lab), deciding which candidate RA-responsive enhancers to test in reporter assays.

ml_idea: Train a frozen-DNA-language-model head on 500 bp sequences to classify RARA/RARB/RXRG/MEIS2 CUT&Tag peaks against GC-matched and H3K27ac-matched background, with chromosome hold-out. Compare against a DR5/DR1 motif scan and test transfer to ReMap cell-line RAR/RXR ChIP-seq.

effort.compute_note: Estimated, not timed: ~150k sequences of 500 bp at ~15/s on CPU for a small DNA language model; logistic or MLP heads on cached embeddings.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Fetch sequences for 2,000 RARA/RARB peaks and 2,000 H3K27ac-only regions and count DR5/DR1 (AGGTCA nnnnn AGGTCA) motifs. No enrichment means the label is accessibility.

verdict_reason: The data is public and clean (verified peak BEDs on GEO GSE325427), but the project is a generic sequence-to-binding task on merged peaks from 2 donors, with no replicate-level data. TF CUT&Tag may largely track open chromatin, and Part C scores below threshold. The Meis2 knockout RNA-seq is 3 vs 3, and its top DEG is Xist, a sex confound, so it is not usable for ML.
